subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class delayed agent-turn lifecycle for provider Batch APIs, and should explicit cron agentTurn jobs be the initial supported surface?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose the permanent public Plugin SDK contract, durable state model, eligible auth/provider modes, or cancellation, fallback, accounting, transcript, and delivery semantics.

options.title: Design cron-first delayed turns
options.body: Approve a generic provider lifecycle and durable state contract, initially exposing it only to explicitly latency-tolerant cron agentTurn jobs.

options.title: Design every background surface
options.body: Cover cron, heartbeat, sessions, and subagents in the initial contract, accepting substantially larger implementation and compatibility scope.

options.title: Decline agent-loop batching
options.body: Keep immediate provider turns as the only core execution mode and leave raw Batch API workflows outside OpenClaw’s tool-using agent loop.

recommendation.title: Design cron-first delayed turns
recommendation.body: Approve a generic provider lifecycle and durable state contract, initially exposing it only to explicitly latency-tolerant cron agentTurn jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined provider/plugin-boundary history and has already participated directly in the issue’s product/API review.
